The varying widths of the 90% confidence intervals directly reflect the escalating uncertainty as the time horizon lengthens. While these confidence intervals are designed to capture the majority of likely outcomes under normal conditions, certain high-impact or "black swan" events could push actual results beyond these stated ranges. On the upside, unexpectedly strong economic data, a significant technological breakthrough, a major policy shift, or a sudden surge in investor confidence could drive the value higher than the upper bounds. Conversely, a severe economic downturn, an escalating geopolitical crisis, a major corporate scandal, an unexpected rise in inflation, or a significant interest rate hike could cause the value to fall below the lower bounds. These extreme scenarios, while not explicitly factored into the primary probabilistic model, represent systemic or unforeseen shocks that can dramatically alter market trajectories, demonstrating the inherent limits of even sophisticated forecasting in the face of truly unprecedented events.
